ApiCtx.description: An api with a request pipeline.

call_imports.description: Deduplicated service clients the route invokes, for imports.

db_imports.description: Comma-joined dependency names for the `from app.db import ..` line.

db_sessions.description: Distinct database sessions the route must inject, in first-use order.

extra_imports.description: Deduplicated ontology getters the route imports, per module.

handlers.description: Deduplicated handlers, in invocation order, for imports.

needs_db.description: Whether any invoked handler needs a database session / cache client.

payload.description: Typed request payload; `None` = untyped JSON body.

CallApiCtx.description: One api of a call target, generated as a client method.

http_method_lower.description: HTTP method for the request, e.g. `post`.

CallTargetCtx.description:
A downstream service this service invokes via `call <Service>.<Api>`:
the compiler generates one typed HTTP client per target.

default_url.description:
Development default: the target's host port from the system
compose mapping, e.g. `http://localhost:8000`.

kebab.description: Compose DNS name of the target's app container, e.g. `billing`.

needs_any.description: Any called api lacks a typed payload (drives dict/Any signatures).

schema_imports.description: Record class names the client file imports.

url_field.description: Settings/Config field holding the base URL, e.g. `billing_url`.

CfgFieldCtx.description: One typed configuration field of an ontology capability instance.

compose_value.description:
Value wired into docker-compose (container DNS), when it differs
from the development default.

rust_default.description:
Rust default literal (all ontology config is `String` in Rust;
numeric/bool values are parsed at the use site).

ChannelCtx.description: A realtime route exposing a stream over WebSocket or SSE.

Ctx.description: Root template context for one deployable project.

call_targets.description: Downstream services invoked via `call`, one typed client each.

dir.description:
Output subdirectory (kebab service name) in multi-service
systems; empty for single-service programs.

events_subject.description: Subject of the default stream backing the legacy `Queue` step.

has_postgres_db.description: Per-engine presence (v0.11 M1), for engine-specific driver deps.

host_port.description: Host port the system docker-compose maps to the app's port 8000.

records_use_datetime.description: Any record uses a `Timestamp` field (drives datetime imports/deps).

records_use_enum.description: Any record uses an inline enum (drives `Literal`/enum declarations).

records_use_json.description: Any record uses a `Json` field (drives `Any` imports).

schema_key_args.description:
Sessionmaker key args for instances that back CRUD resources
(schema creation targets), e.g. [""] or ["\"main\""].

schema_state_fields.description: Rust `AppState` fields for the same schema targets, e.g. ["db"].

table_db_field.description:
Rust `AppState` field of the db instance migrations run against.
`table` declarations aren't bound to a named instance, so this is
always the `default` one; `None` when there is no db instance at
all (i.e. `tables` is also empty).

tables.description:
`table <Name>: <Record>;` declarations: one SQLAlchemy/`FromRow`
model per entry. Schema is provisioned by the v0.7 M5 migration
differ (`ciac-codegen::migrations`), not `create_schema`/
`ensure_schema` — those stay scoped to CRUD resources.

typed_handlers.description:
v0.7 typed handlers (inline body or `extern`) owned by this
service, identified by node id — see the comment at their build
site for why they aren't a `ServiceCtx`.

ExtraDepCtx.description: A capability client a handler receives beyond db/cache.

py_module.description: Python module under `app.` providing the getter.

rust_module.description: Rust module providing the type, e.g. `object_store`.

ExtraImportCtx.description: One `from app.<module> import <getter>` line a route/worker needs.

db_rust_type.description: Rust type as stored in the database (enums are TEXT → `String`).

py_out_type.description:
Python annotation on the read path; enums come back from storage
as their text form, so `Literal[..]` widens to `str`.

type_kind.description:
Language-neutral type, for backends with no dedicated
`<host>_type` field below (v0.10 M1).

FieldTypeKind.description:
A field's language-neutral type (v0.10 M1) — what an *external*
backend maps to its own host language, instead of string-matching
one of the host-specific fields below (the workaround both the
v0.8 Go spike and the first real Go backend had to use, each with
a silent-fallback risk). Mirrors [`ciac_ir::FieldType`]'s closed
set, but lives here so the wire contract doesn't depend on IR
types, and carries the *generated* enum type name rather than raw
variants alone.

db_session.description: The database session this handler consumes, when bound.

extras.description:
Ontology clients this handler receives (object stores, email,
search, external HTTP), resolved to their bound instances.

handler_package.description:
Package the module lives under: `services` for classic/`extern`
handlers (seeded, user-owned), `logic` for v0.7 inline typed
handlers (compiler-owned, lowered from the HIR). Shared by both
backends (Python's `app.<package>`, Rust's `crate::<package>`).

py_args.description:
Precomputed Python constructor arguments for invoking this handler
from a route/worker, e.g. `session=session_main, cache=get_cache("hot")`.
Keeps templates free of whitespace gymnastics.

rust_cache_field.description: Rust `AppState` field for the bound cache, e.g. `cache_hot`.

rust_db_field.description: Rust `AppState` field for the bound database, e.g. `db_main`.

InstanceCtx.description:
One named capability instance (db/cache), with every naming variant
codegen needs. The legacy/`default` instance keeps the unsuffixed
names so pre-v0.4 output is unchanged.

db_engine.description:
Database engine (v0.11 M1): `postgres` | `mysql` for db
instances, empty for caches.

db_user.description:
Compose-container superuser (`postgres` / `root`); doubles as
the dev password, matching the long-standing postgres pattern.

host_port.description:
Host port docker-compose maps for this instance (v0.9 M2), so
the generated system tests can reach it directly from the host:
5432+/3306+ for db instances (per engine), 6379+ for caches —
unique across the whole system, assigned by [`build_system`].

key_arg.description:
Argument for `get_sessionmaker(..)` / `get_cache(..)`:
empty for the default instance, else `"name"` (quoted).

redis_db.description: Redis database index for cache instances (0, 1, ..).

session_dep.description:
FastAPI session dependency (db instances only),
e.g. `get_session` / `get_session_main`.

session_param.description: Route parameter name (db instances only), e.g. `session_main`.

JobCtx.description: A scheduled job with (or without) a processing pipeline.

call_imports.description: Deduplicated service clients the job invokes, for imports.

cron_crate_schedule.description:
`schedule` translated to the `cron` crate's expectations: a leading
seconds field, and weekday `0` (CIaC's Sunday, matching POSIX cron)
rewritten as `7` (the crate only accepts 1-7). Ranges, lists, and
steps in the weekday field are expanded to an explicit list so the
rewrite stays correct across the 0-6/1-7 numbering gap. Rust-only;
other backends parse `schedule` with a library that already accepts
the 0-7 convention.

db_sessions.description: Distinct database sessions the job opens per tick.

extra_imports.description: Deduplicated ontology getters the job imports, per module.

session_with.description:
Pre-joined `async with` items, e.g.
`get_sessionmaker()() as session, get_sessionmaker("main")() as session_main`.

NodeId.description:
Index of a node in a [`SystemGraph`]. Stable for the life of the graph;
nodes are never removed.

`Deserialize` (external-backend protocol M1): a transparent `u32`
newtype with no domain semantics to leak, unlike e.g.
`ciac_ir::FieldType` — safe to round-trip so `Ctx::typed_handlers`
(`ciac-codegen/src/model.rs`), which embeds this directly, can
serialize into the wire contract at all. Note for later milestones:
that field's `NodeId`s are opaque without the `HandlerBody` HIR
they point at (looked up from `NormalizedIr`, not carried in
`SystemModel`) — an external backend can see *that* a typed
handler exists but not what it does, yet.

OntologyInstanceCtx.description:
One instance of an ontology capability (object_store/email/search/
external_http) with its generated-client wiring.

container.description: Compose container name, when a local-dev container exists.

host_port.description:
Host port docker-compose maps for the instance's inspection UI
(email only: the Mailpit web interface).

key_arg.description: Python getter argument: empty for default, else `"media"` (quoted).

PayloadRef.description: The payload type a pipeline (and its handlers) carries.

class_name.description: Record/class name, e.g. `Video`, identical in both targets.

enums.description: Rust needs named enum types; one per inline-enum field.

has_id.description:
Whether the record declares its own `id` field. Typed CRUD always
stores a server-generated TEXT `id` primary key; when the record
has one it doubles as that key, otherwise one is synthesized.

is_error.description:
`error` (v0.7) vs. plain `record`: an error record generates a
raisable exception type instead of a `BaseModel`.

name.description: Type name in both targets, e.g. `Video`.

select_cols.description:
Precomputed SQL fragments for typed CRUD, e.g.
`id, title, status` / `$1, $2, $3` / `title = $2, status = $3`.

db_session.description: Session dependency backing this resource's store.

plural.description: Route base and table name, e.g. `notes`.

record.description:
Typed columns from `crud <Name>: <Record>;`; `None` keeps the
generic keyed-document model.

rust_db_field.description: Rust `AppState` fields for the bound instances.

payload.description:
Payload type when every pipeline using this handler agrees on one;
`None` falls back to untyped JSON.

rust_db_field.description: Rust `AppState` fields for the bound db/cache instances.

SessionCtx.description: A database session a route/worker needs for its handlers.

subject.description: Subject of the published stream, for `publish` steps.

SystemModel.description:
The generated system: one deployable project per declared service, or
a single unprefixed project for single-service programs.

has_db.description: Any service declares databases (drives the compose volume list).

has_queue.description:
Any service publishes/consumes streams (the system compose then
runs one shared broker every service's `nats_url` points at).

multi.description:
True when the program declares `service { .. }` blocks; the
backends then emit each service under `<dir>/` plus root
docker-compose/README files for the whole system.

TableCtx.description:
A resolved `table <Name>: <Record>;` declaration, ready for a
SQLAlchemy model: same field data as [`RecordCtx`], named after the
table (not the record) so a record reused under several table names
doesn't collide.

WorkerCtx.description: A declared worker with (or without) a processing pipeline.

call_imports.description: Deduplicated service clients the worker invokes, for imports.

db_sessions.description: Distinct database sessions the worker opens per message.

extra_imports.description: Deduplicated ontology getters the worker imports, per module.

queue_group.description: Queue group so replicas of this worker load-balance.

session_with.description:
Pre-joined `async with` items, e.g.
`get_sessionmaker()() as session, get_sessionmaker("main")() as session_main`.

request.description:
Everything an external backend needs to generate a project for one
`--target`, serialized as the request payload.

target.description:
The `--target` name the request was built for (informational at
this stage — nothing branches on it yet, since `SystemModel` is
already target-neutral).

request.title: CodegenRequest

FileRole.description: Regeneration ownership role for a generated file.

oneOf.description: Compiler-owned wiring. Regeneration may rewrite it when unchanged.
Generated seed owned by the user after first write.

response.description:
What an external backend writes to its own stdout after reading a
[`CodegenRequest`] from stdin: the generated file tree, in exactly
the shape [`crate::GeneratedProject`] already uses internally, plus
`protocol_version` so [`crate::external::ExternalBackend`] can
refuse a response from a backend built against an incompatible
contract instead of silently misinterpreting it.
response.title: CodegenResponse
